title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Introduction
This project analyzes global temperature change from 1901 through the most recent data available from the NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS).
The analysis examines temperature change from several complementary perspectives, including long-term temporal trends, statistical distributions, hemispheric differences, latitude zones, seasonal patterns, surface-area distributions, and global spatial patterns.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Temperature Anomalies
Temperature change is expressed using temperature anomalies rather than absolute temperatures. An anomaly represents the difference between an observed temperature and a reference-period average.
The NASA GISTEMP data used in this project express temperature anomalies relative to the 1951–1980 baseline. This reference baseline is retained throughout the analysis so that all reported anomaly values have a consistent interpretation.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Climate Periods
The analysis groups observations into consecutive 30-year climate periods beginning in 1901. The use of 30-year periods follows the climatological convention used by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).



Climate Period
Years




1
1901–1930


2
1931–1960


3
1961–1990


4
1991–2020


5
2021–Present



The final climate period is incomplete and extends through the most recent data available.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Workflow
The analysis is organized as a reproducible workflow consisting of three stages:

Data Acquisition
Download the latest NASA GISTEMP temperature data and Natural Earth coastline data, and document the project software environment and acquired datasets.
Data Transformation
Clean, transform, aggregate, and spatially prepare the source data; calculate grid-cell areas; and save reusable transformed datasets.
Data Visualization
Create statistical summaries and visualizations examining global time series, climate-period distributions, hemispheres, latitude zones, seasons, surface-area distributions, and global gridded temperature patterns.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Data
Temperature data are obtained from the NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP) project.
The source data used in this analysis include:

Global monthly temperature anomalies
Northern Hemisphere monthly temperature anomalies
Southern Hemisphere monthly temperature anomalies
Latitude-zone annual temperature anomalies
Global gridded monthly temperature anomalies in NetCDF format

The global coastline is obtained from Natural Earth and is used as a geographic reference layer for the global maps.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Software
Programming Language: R
Development Environment: Positron
Document Creation: Quarto
R Packages:

gt – summary tables
ncdf4 – NetCDF processing
pals – diverging color palettes
patchwork – plot layouts
rnaturalearth – geographic coastline data
R.utils – gzip decompression
sf – spatial data processing
tidyverse – data manipulation and visualization
viridisLite – sequential color palettes

Exact software and package versions used for the project are documented in the Data Acquisition chapter.

title: Data Acquisition
text:
Download temperature anomalies

Download csv files


Code
for (i in seq_len(nrow(file_catalog))) {

  if (file_catalog$format[[i]] == "CSV") {

    filename <- file_catalog$filename[[i]]
    source_url <- file_catalog$source_url[[i]]

    download_path <- paste0(
      source_url,
      filename
    )

    latest_path <- file.path(
      dir_raw,
      filename
    )

    archive_path <- file.path(
      dir_archive,
      filename
    )

    download.file(
      url = download_path,
      destfile = latest_path,
      mode = "wb",
      quiet = TRUE
    )

    file.copy(
      from = latest_path,
      to = archive_path,
      overwrite = TRUE
    )

    message(
      "Updated: ",
      filename
    )
  }
}




Download netCDF file


Code
for (i in seq_len(nrow(file_catalog))) {
  if (file_catalog$format[[i]] == "NetCDF") {
    filename <- file_catalog$filename[[i]]
    source_url <- file_catalog$source_url[[i]]
    download_path <- paste0(
      source_url,
      filename,
      ".gz"
    )
    latest_path <- file.path(
      dir_raw,
      filename
    )
    archive_path <- file.path(
      dir_archive,
      paste0(
        filename,
        ".gz"
      )
    )
    temporary_path <- paste0(
      archive_path,
      ".download"
    )
    download.file(
      url = download_path,
      destfile = temporary_path,
      mode = "wb",
      quiet = FALSE
    )
    file.rename(
      from = temporary_path,
      to = archive_path
    )
    R.utils::gunzip(
      filename = archive_path,
      destname = latest_path,
      overwrite = TRUE,
      remove = FALSE
    )
  }
}




Acquire coastline


Code
path_coastline <- file.path(dir_raw,"global-coastline.gpkg")
coastline_sf <- rnaturalearth::ne_download(
  scale = 10,
  type = "coastline",
  category = "physical",
  returnclass = "sf"
)
sf::st_write(
  coastline_sf,
  path_coastline,
  layer = "coastline",
  delete_dsn = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE
)
file_catalog <-
  bind_rows(
    file_catalog,
    tibble(
      dataset = "Global Coastline",
      source = "Natural Earth",
      format = "GeoPackage",
      filename = basename(
        path_coastline
      ),
      source_url =
        "https://www.naturalearthdata.com/",
      local_path = path_coastline
    )
  )




Update catalog

file_catalog <-
  file_catalog |>
  mutate(
    directory = dirname(

    ),

      "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
    ),

Create catalog


Code
transformed_catalog <- tibble(
  path = list.files(
    dir_transformed,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
) |>
  filter(
    !file.info(path)$isdir
  ) |>
  mutate(
    filename = basename(path),
    format = tools::file_ext(filename),
    directory = dirname(path),
    transformation_datetime = format(
      file.info(path)$mtime,
      "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
    ),
    file_size_kb = round(
      file.info(path)$size / 1024,
      0
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(
    transformed_descriptions,
    by = "filename"
  ) |>
  arrange(filename) |>
  select(
    dataset,
    filename,
    format,
    directory,
    transformation_datetime,
    file_size_kb

v2_statistics <- df_glb_mth |>
  group_by(climate_period) |>
  summarize(
    median = median(anomaly, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(anomaly, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(anomaly, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = IQR(anomaly, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower_fence = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper_fence = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    outliers = sum(
      anomaly < lower_fence |
      anomaly > upper_fence,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

v2_statistics_table <- v2_statistics |>
  select(
    climate_period,
    median,
    q1,
    q3,
    iqr,
    outliers
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -climate_period,
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    statistic = recode(
      statistic,
      median = "Median",
      q1 = "Q1 (25th percentile)",

Code
weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs) {
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w)
  x <- x[keep]
  w <- w[keep]
  ord <- order(x)
  x <- x[ord]
  w <- w[ord]
  cumulative_weight <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  sapply(
    probs,
    function(p) {
      x[which(cumulative_weight >= p)[1]]
    }
  )
}

  summarize(

      weighted.mean(
        avg_anomaly,

      median(
        avg_anomaly,
        na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_area_above_0 =
      100 *
      sum(
        area_km2[avg_anomaly > 0],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        area_km2[!is.na(avg_anomaly)],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    pct_area_above_1 =
      100 *
      sum(
        area_km2[avg_anomaly > 1],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        area_km2[!is.na(avg_anomaly)],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop")

  pivot_longer(
    cols = -climate_period,
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "value"

  mutate(
    statistic = recode(
      statistic,
      area_weighted_mean = "Area-weighted mean anomaly",
      median_anomaly = "Median cell anomaly",
      pct_area_above_0 = "Observed area above 0 °C",
      pct_area_above_1 = "Observed area above 1 °C"),
